question: Why are moons and asteroids smaller than a few hundred kilometres lumpy, while bigger ones are round?
answer: Because at that size gravity beats the strength of rock. A body's pull on its own surface grows with its size, and past a few hundred kilometres it can crush its high points down, the way a tall sandcastle slumps. Icy bodies give way at a smaller size than rocky ones, because ice is softer.
move: Size changes which force wins, so big things follow different rules.
ask: In my work, at what size does a project start obeying different rules from when it was small?
reference: Lineweaver & Norman, The Potato Radius: a Lower Minimum Size for Dwarf Planets, arXiv:1004.1091, 2010
